note: Year-round full-hookup RV park on the north side of Story City, near I-35, with gravel pull-throughs; many sites are let by the week or month to long-stay residents. Self check-in at an unstaffed lobby; propane refills and firewood sold. No ATVs or dirt bikes. --Claude
summary: Operator site (2026): $45 nightly (+$5 by card), weekly $240, monthly $620, full hookups 20/30/50 A, laundry, showers, dump, open year round, reservations by text/call/email only. Google 4.0 (138). Long-stay leaning; nightly stays are real (four 2026 overnight reviews on RV Life). Borderline on the long-stay rule, not an automatic drop.
flags: GATE: cheapest nightly $45 cash or $50 by card ('NIGHTLY CREDIT CARD FEE - $5') - at the $50 line, not over it. No gateway within 40 km (gateways.py: nearest St. Paul 309 km). Good Sam: stored false. Presence: live operator site with phone 515-231-9430; Google Maps 4.0 from 138 reviews (1011 Timberland Dr, Story City, phone the same).

LONG-STAY (five tests): (1) share of nightly sites - not published; Campendium 2023 review (Mn-Wander, 3.0, $30): 'Mostly full timers.'; RV Life June 2026 review (Motorhome, $40, site 33, rating 10): 'As it seems most RV parks these days are relying more and more to permanent residents. This park is no exception, they do however seem to want to keep the park clean and looking good.' Imagery shows ~45-50 occupied pads, many with sheds/vehicles. (2) Posted nightly rate: yes, $45, on the operator page - passes. (3) Booking: text/call/email only, no engine; RV Life June 2026: 'All reservations are done via email. Check-in is done at the unmanned Check-in Lobby.' (4) Nightly use: RV Life lists four 2026 overnight stays on pull-throughs 32-35 ($40-45), so well over 1 site in 10 is sold nightly - passes. (5) No homes or memberships sold - passes. Operator wording leans residential: 'A late fee of $25 will be assessed if payment is late', 'forfeiture of any prepaid rent', '2 adults per site'. Other review: RV Life Oct 2026 (rating 4/10, $45): 'No picnic table fire pit and packed in like sardines'.

MY READ: borderline - a long-stay-leaning park that does sell real overnight nights at a posted rate, with Google at exactly 4.0 (not under 4, so the automatic drop does not apply) and price at $45-50. On the AWH 2026-10-31 rule (on the fence + mostly seasonal + iffy = drop) this is a judgement call for AWH; I would keep it with the note's long-stay line, but it is a fair drop candidate if AWH reads it as mostly long-stay.
